Excluded entities don't need owners identified, and nonprofits still need a control person, so the rule has to account for both.

I'm now checking how excluded owners feed into the unaccounted share: an excluded owner under 25% doesn't get the same exemption as one at 25% or more, so its share may still need identified individuals. I'm considering adding that portion to the unaccounted total, which would mean summing those smaller excluded shares and treating the result as part of the completeness check.

I'm weighing whether an unaccounted share of 25% or more should make ownership incomplete on its own, since the SOP is about whether an unidentified person could reach 25%. I'm leaning toward treating the unaccounted total as the decisive test, with excluded owners under 25% folded into that total.

I'm weighing whether to drop counts_when and write the identification test into each screening rule, since a "some" over the people list can't see unidentified owners with modest stakes. Doing so would let an unidentified 20% holder combined with the unaccounted share be checked against the 25% threshold, which seems closer to the SOP's wording.

I'm deciding to keep the identified-individuals collection as the control person plus anyone at 25% or more, and I'm leaving the unidentified small-owner case aside for now.

I'm also checking section 2.1's most-severe-wins ordering and section 2.2's rule that unknown facts block approval.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.unknown_when_empty: who the identified individuals are (the control person, and every individual who owns 25% or more unless the entity is a nonprofit)
people.text: Entities on the excluded list do not require beneficial owners to be identified. ... For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. ... Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.
Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is the outcome when no rule applies; Incomplete comes from the unknowns handling (2.2).
Sets the order: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets the unknowns outcome: a rule that might apply because a fact is unknown leads to incomplete.
Excluded entities have no identified individuals. This is handled by the people list's counts_when (excluded is no) and empty_ok_when (excluded is yes). It also gates the rules for 3.2 and 3.3.
The control person is an identified individual. This is set in the people list's counts_when.

Owners of 25% or more are identified individuals unless the entity is a nonprofit (counts_when). The open share is unaccounted_pct plus shares held by excluded entities that own less than 25%, because the exemption covers only excluded owners of 25% or more (computed open_pct). The SOP's test is that 'no unidentified person could own 25% or more'. As translated, it checks only whether the open share alone reaches 25%. A known owner below 25% who could also hold part of the open share is not checked. A person should decide whether the SOP means this.
The materiality bar is applied by the pack in entity_adverse_media and adverse_media. The search-recording requirement has no fact (see needs).
This contradicts 5.2. Under 2.1, 5.2's escalate always outranks this approve, so this rule can never decide a case. It is translated as written, and a person should resolve the conflict.
An individual's location is taken as residence.
An individual's location is taken as residence.
